title: I vibe coded a muggle quidditch game trailer
author: BuildMeATeam
selftext:
Codex/Claude to get started, Codex to make most of the trailer itself (didn't open a video editor) and then Gemini music for the trailer!  
Try it out, happy to get feedback: [trihoop.com](http://trihoop.com)

comments.author: Useful_Use_6170
comments.body: Nice how did you make the trailer?!? It’s nice

replies.author: BuildMeATeam
replies.body: I created the game, had 2 AIs face off, screen captured, then asked claude to make a series of sequences that I adaped based on the feel. Music was also original in Gemini! I liked it so much the new version of the game uses music now.

comments.author: Savings_Cloud5486
comments.body: How did you implement ai movement?

replies.author: BuildMeATeam
replies.body:
Hi, I started simple and built up complexity and spent time learning about what were the key metrics that would let me improve it. Those are full AI-vs-AI simulations. I've been working on making the game more "cinematic" and planning to make a youtube series just because it ends up being fun to watch (for me, anyway).

[https://www.youtube.com/@BuildMeATeam](https://www.youtube.com/@BuildMeATeam)  
The BuildMeATeam brand is another project I'm working on, and so I thought a game would drive traffic to that site, so the game advertises that name a bit :).

comments.author: jeebiuss
comments.body: How long it take you to make

replies.author: BuildMeATeam
replies.body: Making the game zero->launch, about 15 hours of active work. The video, 4 hours. Tweaks and balancing, its been about +4 h each night. Working in the low paid tier was slow but i thought carefully how to proceed, then i got obsessed, upgraded, now my productivity dropped a lot despite no limits... I'm also at a more compl;icated stage and that is hard to vibe change without bugs. I'm more focused on making the controls feel better since about tuesday... :)
